_readme: The sidebar, the prev/next pager, the catalog cards, chapter numbering, <title>/SEO meta and sitemap.xml are all generated from this file. After editing, run: SITE_ROOT=en node scripts/build_nav.js. In-chapter anchor titles live in each HTML file's <section data-nav="...">. The `part` field decides the grouping headings on the catalog page and in the sidebar. Human-readable fields are translation units tracked in i18n/ledger.json.

site.title: Home Assistant Cloudflared Web GUI guide
site.subtitle: No open ports, a safe way home
site.description: 12-chapter Cloudflared Web GUI guide: install, Setup, Cloudflare authorization, hostname, Dashboard, Config, Logs, security and troubleshooting.
site.footerMeta: Screenshots are from Home Assistant and the Cloudflared Web GUI. Home Assistant and Cloudflare are trademarks of their respective owners; this site is not affiliated with either.

strings._readme: This site's pager labels carry mdi arrow icons (a leftover from the old generator); the remaining chrome strings use the kit defaults. Keep the icon markup; translate only the words.

chrome._readme: No empty "Appendices" block in the sidebar/catalog when there are no appendices; catalog groups after the first use class chapter-index-spaced (defined in style.css) instead of an inline style.

hub._readme: index.html is the four-way Resource Hub, maintained by hand; build_nav does not touch it. The tutorial catalog page is generated by build_nav into the file named by `catalog`. `pages` are the standalone single-file handbooks under the hub (each carries its own head and styles); they are included in sitemap.xml and in the check_links allowlist.

chapters.navLabel: Before you start: requirements and security boundaries
chapters.title: Before you start
chapters.card: First confirm your domain, Cloudflare DNS, your Home Assistant installation type, and the locally or remotely managed mode.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI, planning before you start: your Cloudflare domain, Home Assistant add-ons, tunnel mode and security boundaries.

chapters.title: Install the Web GUI
chapters.card: Add the WoowTech repository to the Apps store, install the add-on and leave it in a safe initial state.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Cloudflared Web GUI install guide: add the repository, install the add-on and check everything before you start it.

chapters.navLabel: First open of the Web GUI
chapters.title: First open
chapters.pagerTitle: 03 · First open of the Web GUI
chapters.card: Open the interface through Home Assistant Ingress and get to know Dashboard, Setup, Config and Logs.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI first open: Ingress, the four main pages and a read-only status check.

chapters.title: Setup wizard
chapters.card: Use the wizard to sort out the hostname, the tunnel mode and the authorization prerequisites, and do not rush to hit apply.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI Setup wizard: first-run configuration, local tunnel and getting ready to authorize.

chapters.title: Cloudflare authorization
chapters.card: Recognize the one-time authorization URL, pick the right domain, and avoid leaking the account certificate or the authorization link.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Tunnel: the Cloudflare authorization flow, the safety points to watch and how to run the acceptance check.

chapters.title: Dashboard status
chapters.card: Learn to read the tunnel, edge connections and add-on status; observe first, then decide whether to act.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI Dashboard: tunnel status, edge connections and security checks.

chapters.title: Config settings
chapters.card: Understand how the Web GUI and Supervisor options stay in sync, and tell apart the scope of impact of each setting.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI Config: Supervisor options, tunnel_name, log_level and safe configuration.

chapters.title: External hostname
chapters.card: Plan the Home Assistant public hostname, the trusted proxy and the end-to-end acceptance check.
chapters.description: A guide to setting Cloudflared external_hostname and Home Assistant trusted_proxies.

chapters.title: Additional hosts
chapters.card: Expose only the local services you really need, and understand hostname, service and the DNS cleanup after a deletion.
chapters.description: Cloudflared additional_hosts guide: service forwarding, minimal exposure and DNS cleanup.

chapters.title: Logs and maintenance
chapters.card: Use the live log, filtering and download to build a repeatable health-check routine.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI Logs, routine maintenance, version updates and safe log handling.

chapters.title: Security checks
chapters.card: Check the entrance, accounts, hostname, DNS and the Zero Trust boundary so convenience does not turn into over-exposure.
chapters.description: Cloudflare Tunnel and Home Assistant: security checks, minimal exposure and the Zero Trust boundary.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting and handover
chapters.card: Work through HA, the Web GUI, cloudflared, DNS and the Cloudflare edge in order, and leave a record you can hand over.
chapters.description: Cloudflared Web GUI troubleshooting: HA Ingress, the tunnel, DNS, Logs, updates and handover.

i18n._readme: hreflang is what the zh pages use to point at themselves; xDefault says which locale to point at (en or primary), and can be flipped in one line. The locale list is in i18n/locales.json.
